description: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 and lower ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48, which gives base_dim 480 and rounds up to model_dim 512 (4 heads of 128), so the model is two layers deeper at the same width; WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" applies cleanly to 10 layers.
Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 to spend more time in the low-learning-rate regime.
Switch WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "LLLL" so every attention layer uses full causal context instead of half-context sliding windows on three of four layers.
Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^20 and adjust gradient accumulation steps to fit within the time budget, potentially stabilizing gradients at lower batch per step.
Applies an incorrect, broken edit that attempts to implement per-layer depth-based LR decay but introduces a syntax error, so it is aborted.
Zero-initialize the attention and MLP output projections, which is already the case in the current train.py, so no edit is proposed.
Replace the Adam optimizer for the token embedding parameters with Lion (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, sign-based update) using a smaller learning rate, keeping Adam for other non-matrix groups.

issues: The candidate only adds a docstring to adamw_step_fused. It doesn't change behaviour, so any difference from the incumbent is run-to-run noise. Spending a slot on it was a waste.

No integrity problems: the diff doesn't touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the prepare.py import line, the seed lines or the evaluation call. A docstring inside a torch.compile(fullgraph=True) function is harmless.

Can't recompute z exactly: the incumbent standard deviation and the unrounded values aren't given. The reported z = -0.012 fits the numbers given: the candidate is 0.0001 worse (1.1146 vs 1.1145), which implies an incumbent spread of about 0.008. Because the values are rounded, that estimate is loose.
The provisional decision to reject is right: one run with essentially no change gives no evidence of improvement.

description: The crash is a NameError because `_step_adamw` calls `adamw_step_fused`, which is never defined; the file instead defines a broken `lion_step_fused` in its place, so I replace that function with a standard fused AdamW step under the expected name.
Set torch.compile on the model to mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" (keeping dynamic=False) to try for higher steps per second in the fixed 300 s window, without changing model math.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to double the number of optimizer steps, increasing updates on the small model within the 300s budget.
Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 to test if a higher learning rate for Muon optimizer produces better results within the fixed time budget.
Train on half-length sequences (batch reshaped to 2x batch at T/2, same tokens per step) for the first 30% of the time budget, then switch to full 2048 context.
Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine schedule to more smoothly decay the learning rate towards the final fraction.
Increase matrix learning rate to leverage more of the 300s budget per step by making up more parameter updates before dropout.
Aborted: the MLP in train.py already uses squared ReLU (F.relu(x).square()), so the requested change would be a no-op.

issues: Nothing found in category (1). The diff does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the prepare.py import line, the seed lines, the evaluation call or the summary printing.

Nothing found in category (2). The diff adds a per-head sigmoid output gate: out_gate is a Linear from n_embd to n_head, applied as y * sigmoid(out_gate(x)).unsqueeze(-1). The (B,T,H,1) gate broadcasts correctly over y's (B,T,H,D) shape before the reshape. The gate weight starts at zero, so every gate starts at 0.5 and attention output is halved at init. That is a design choice, not a bug. I assume the existing optimizer grouping picks up the new parameter as a 2D matrix in the blocks. If out_gate fell into a group with an unsuitable LR, results would degrade, but they would still be a valid measurement.

The numbers are consistent with each other. The candidate scored 1.0994 against the incumbent's 1.0942, which is 0.0052 worse (lower is better). A negative z matches the candidate being worse. The reported z of -0.674 implies a noise sigma of about 0.0077 per difference. The noise model is not given, so the size of z cannot be checked independently.

Each side has only one run, so the comparison carries little evidence. Even so, the candidate is worse by the point estimate, and the provisional reject is the right call. The candidate also adds code and parameters without a gain, which the simplicity rule disfavours.

description: Add a per-head sigmoid output gate (zero-initialized Linear(model_dim, n_head) computed from the normalized attention input) applied to the flash-attention output before the output projection.
Switch optimizer steps every 90 seconds of the training budget, using a smaller batch early and a larger batch later.

Keep a float32 EMA (decay 0.999) of all model parameters, updated after each optimizer step, and copy the EMA weights into the live parameters just before the final evaluation so the harness scores the averaged model.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 to provide a short linear warmup period for the embeddings and scalar parameters.
Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 to test if maintaining a small residual learning rate during the final warmdown phase improves the final val_bpb.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff only changes the training loss to a cross-entropy weighted by bytes per token. It leaves the evaluation call, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import line and the summary printing alone. Matching the training objective to the bits-per-byte metric is a legitimate change.

The byte lengths are not exact. Decoding each token on its own breaks byte-fallback or partial UTF-8 tokens: they decode to U+FFFD, which counts as 3 bytes. Special tokens like BOS get a nonzero weight from their text form, while the official metric gives them 0 bytes. The weights will be slightly off, but the result is still meaningful.
`model.byte_lens = byte_lens` is never used, because the loss reads the global `byte_lens`. It's dead code; remove it to keep things simple.

The loss is now computed outside the compiled model, from full logits with reduction='none'. That likely adds some memory and time compared with the fused in-model loss, so check VRAM and step throughput at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64.

This assumes `model(x)` with no targets returns logits of shape (B, T, V), and that `F`, `vocab_size`, `tokenizer` and `device` are defined at this point in train.py. Check this, since the candidate was a lint repair.
There are no GPU numbers yet, so z can't be computed and there are no claims to check.

description: Weight each token's training cross-entropy by its UTF-8 byte length (from decoding each id with the imported tokenizer) and normalize by the batch's byte total, so the training loss matches the bits-per-byte metric; only the training call is changed and evaluation is untouched.

The run hit CUDA OOM in backward because the per-micro-batch fp32 logits (64 x 2048 x 8192 vocab) and their activations exceed the A100 40 GB; halving DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 fits in memory and doubles grad accumulation to 4, leaving the effective TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE of 2^18 tokens unchanged.
